visual.detailed_description: Portrait photograph (taken with a phone) of a monitor showing a grayscale sagittal CT reformat of the lower spine in a bone-type window. The vertebral column runs from the top of the frame toward the lower right; the vertebral bodies lie to the left of a dark, narrow spinal-canal band and the posterior elements (spinous processes and facet regions) lie to its right, so anterior is toward the left of the image. Three red arrows with red text labels "L1" (upper left, pointing at the anterior margin of a vertebral body), "L4" (lower left) and "L5" (just below L4) are superimposed. The vertebral body at the L1 arrow has a trapezoidal profile that appears narrower anteriorly; the bodies at the L4 and L5 arrows show irregular, concave-looking endplates and mixed trabecular density. Bowel loops, including a rounded air-filled loop, are visible at the left edge and the sacrum is seen at the lower right. The word "Lossy" is overlaid at the bottom center and a small unreadable symbol sits at the top center. Faint screen moire and glare are present from photographing the display.
